full_judgment: 267. The fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence is that the accused is presumed to be innocent unless contrary is proved. Thus the contrary proof is the heavy burden upon the prosecution to rebut the presumption leading cogent evidence as to the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
